title: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in preparing and serving food.

tasks.text: Resolve customer complaints regarding food service.
Train workers in food preparation, and in service, sanitation, and safety procedures.
Assign duties, responsibilities, and work stations to employees in accordance with work requirements.
Present bills and accept payments.
Perform various financial activities, such as cash handling, deposit preparation, and payroll.
Supervise and participate in kitchen and dining area cleaning activities.
Recommend measures for improving work procedures and worker performance to increase service quality and enhance job safety.
Specify food portions and courses, production and time sequences, and workstation and equipment arrangements.
Control inventories of food, equipment, smallware, and liquor, and report shortages to designated personnel.
Observe and evaluate workers and work procedures to ensure quality standards and service, and complete disciplinary write-ups.
Analyze operational problems, such as theft and wastage, and establish procedures to alleviate these problems.
Inspect supplies, equipment, and work areas to ensure efficient service and conformance to standards.
Greet and seat guests, and present menus and wine lists.
Evaluate new products for usefulness and suitability.
Compile and balance cash receipts at the end of the day or shift.
Forecast staff, equipment, and supply requirements, based on a master menu.
Assess nutritional needs of patients, plan special menus, supervise the assembly of regular and special diet trays, and oversee the delivery of food trolleys to hospital patients.
Record production, operational, and personnel data on specified forms.

Perform personnel actions, such as hiring and firing staff, providing employee orientation and training, and conducting supervisory activities, such as creating work schedules or organizing employee time sheets.
Estimate ingredients and supplies required to prepare a recipe.
Purchase or requisition supplies and equipment needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of services.
Perform food preparation and serving duties, such as carving meat, preparing flambe dishes, or serving wine and liquor.
Schedule parties and take reservations.
Develop departmental objectives, budgets, policies, procedures, and strategies.
Conduct meetings and collaborate with other personnel for menu planning, serving arrangements, and related details.
Develop equipment maintenance schedules and arrange for repairs.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Evernote, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel, Restaurant Operations & Management Spreadsheet Library.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Microsoft Project.
